title: Decision-gate opponent-seat gradient conflict audit
benchmark: A frozen learned policy plays at least 100,000 fresh 200bb HUNL Slumbot hands, scores above 0 bb/100, and has a 95% confidence-interval lower bound above 0.
hypothesis: The high-dose gate's residual opponent/seat failures arise from material conflict among the twelve opponent-seat policy gradients; replaying the exact saved transitions will show negative ordinary worst-group alignment while an MGDA minimum-norm direction is nonnegative for every group.
material_change: Replay all twelve saved transition shards from exact seed initializations and Adam state, verify endpoint reconstruction, and at each of four pre-update points per seed compute the twelve full policy-gradient vectors, pairwise cosines, ordinary alignment, and MGDA alignment. No new game, policy rollout, or environment hand.
baseline: Ordinary equal-weight average policy gradient used by the completed high-dose run.
notes: Admission of one separately preregistered MGDA-gate comparison requires endpoint replay max tensor error <=1e-6 in all seeds, pairwise negative conflicts, ordinary worst-group alignment <0 in at least half of the 12 chunk audits, MGDA worst-group alignment >=-1e-8 in every chunk, and strict MGDA improvement in every chunk. Otherwise close the decision-gate route.
Exact replay counted 32655 source transitions across twelve shards; corrects the preregistered manual total 32455 without changing any source artifact.

result.summary: Exact replay consumed all 32,655 saved transitions and reconstructed all three high-dose gate endpoints bit-exactly. Every one of 12 chunk audits had material conflict: 20-38 negative gradient pairs, pairwise minimum cosine -0.977 to -0.783, and ordinary worst-group alignment -0.962 to -0.118. MGDA improved every chunk to positive worst-group alignment +0.0396 to +0.2317 with broad 7-12 group support.
result.conclusion: The high-dose gate's remaining opponent/seat weakness has a concrete optimization mechanism: equal averaging applies a direction opposed to at least one opponent-seat objective at every update point, while an MGDA common descent direction exists throughout. This is exact saved-transition geometry, not strength evidence, and justifies one matched on-policy MGDA gate smoke only.
result.next_step: Run a separately preregistered three-seed MGDA-gate treatment matched to the high-dose ordinary arm in frozen experts, seeds, decks, hand budgets, learning rate, epochs, KL, and evaluation. Require exact evidence, positive worst-group training alignment at every step, and the original multi-seed/opponent/seat holdout breadth gates before any geometric scaling.
